To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) robot errors have an effect on human perceptions of trust and reliability, but not on their decision to comply with the robot's requests; (2) task irreversibility is the most influential factor in determining participants' compliance; and (3) personality traits do not seem to affect the decision to comply, although they may affect the subjective assessment of the robot and the trust in it.

(1) participants' trust in the robot and their willingness to follow its requests is not significantly affected by its erroneous behavior and (2) their interaction choices and decisions are influenced by the nature of the robot's task requests.

(1) robot performance does not seem substantially influence participants' willingness to comply with the robot's requests; (2) the task requested by robot has an impact on participants' decision to follow its instructions; and (3) participants' personality traits have an impact on their willingness to comply with a robot's requests.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of robot performance on the human perception and acceptance of the robot, as well as the impact of the task type on the decision to comply with its requests, and provides a better understanding of the role that trust and personality may play in human-robot interaction.

a faulty robot is not necessarily a less trustworthy or less acceptable robot.
, while the robot's performance may affect participants' perception of it, it does not seem to have a significant influence on their decisions to (not to) follow its requests.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nature of a task, rather than the robot's reliability, determines participants' willingness to comply with its instructions.
, while the perception of robot's performance may have an impact on its trustworthiness, its actual performance does not necessarily affect human behavior and decisions in human-robot interactions.
, while the robot's performance is a significant predictor of its perceived reliability and trustworthinnes, the latter are not necessarily good predictors of human-robot interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to successfully integrate robots into our everyday lives, we need to better understand their influence on our behavior and how we perceive them.
, in order for robots to be accepted and trusted by humans, they should be designed to avoid mistakes that may have irreversible consequences.
the effects of robot performance on human behavior are complex and depend on a number of factors, including task type and personality.
